## Halaman 1596 — Section (`Hal-1596`)

10H-16 Communication System: K14B Model
Troubleshooting
> **NOTE**
• Before diagnosing trouble, be sure to check equipment of vehicle being serviced as well as control
modules and sensor connected to CAN communication line.
• Before using scan tool, read its “Operator’s (I nstruction) Manual” to know how to use it.
• When performing “Communication Bus Check” using SUZUKI scan tool in this troubleshooting,
refer to “Judgment of Communication Bus Check”: K14B Model (Page 10H-18).
Step Action Yes No
1 CAN communication circuit check
1) Disconnect negative (–) cable at battery.
2) Disconnect connectors from all the control modules and
sensor communicating by CAN. )(Page 10H-12)
3) Check for proper connection to each CAN
communication circuit at all control module / sensor
(communicating by CAN) connectors and DLC.
4) If connections are OK, check the following points of each
CAN communication circuit based on results found in
Steps 3) of “Diagnosis Procedure”: K14B Model (Page
10H-13).
• Open circuit
• Short to power circuit
• Short to ground circuit
• Short to CAN communication wire with each other
Is check result OK?
Go to Step 2. Repair or replace
defective wire harness.
2 ECM terminating resistance check
1) Connect “E01” connector to ECM.
2) Measure resistance between the following terminals.
• Without ABS: “E04-4” and “E04-11” terminals of BCM
connector
• With ABS: “E24-3” and “2 4-16” terminals of ABS
control module connector
Is resistance 114 to 134 Ω?
Go to Step 3. Replace ECM and
recheck DTC. )(Page
1C-1)
3 Combination meter terminating resistance check
1) Connect connector to combination meter.
2) Measure resistance between “G211-6” and “G211-14”
terminals of DLC.
Is resistance 114 to 134 Ω?
Go to Step 4. Replace combination
meter and recheck
DTC. )(Page 9C-9)
4 Combination meter, P/S control module, BCM, ABS
control module (ABS model) and ECM communication
check
1) Connect connectors to P/S control module, BCM and
ABS control module (ABS model).
2) Connect negative (–) cable at battery.
3) Set ignition “ON”.

## Halaman 1600 — Section (`Hal-1600`)

10H-20 Communication System: D13A Model
D13A Model
Precautions
Precautions for Diagnosing Trouble
AENBL80AA820001
• Before using SUZUKI scan tool, read its “Operator’ s (Instructions) Manual” to know how to use it.
• Diagnosing target control module / sensor only is not enough in order to accurately diagnose any trouble of CAN
communication system. Check communication conditions of overall system (including control modules and sensor
related in CAN communication) and diagnose trouble by putting those information together.
• It may be possible that CAN system has trouble beca use of blown fuse or low battery voltage. Before
troubleshooting, confirm that fuse, battery voltage and charging system condition are normal.
• CAN communication error is detected if connector of control modules or sensor being connected to CAN
communication line or applicable fuse is connected / disconnected when ignition is “ON”.
• Confirm that no equipment or option other than original parts is connected onto CAN bus. If any of those items are
connected, disconnect it before troubleshooting.
• If any DTCs together with “Lost Communication” (Reception  error) and/or “Communication Bus Off” are displayed,
start troubleshooting of CAN communication first.
• Before diagnosing trouble, be sure to check equipment of vehicle being serviced as well as control modules and
sensor connected to CAN communication line.
• Be sure to clear all DTCs after completing troubleshooting.
General Description
Communication System Description
AENBL80AA821001
System Description
Communication for each control module and device is established through continuous input / output of ON/OFF
signals with various data items being managed in parallel. Transmitting / receiving these data is called as serial
communication interface.
A serial communication interface that is CAN protocol (a communication standard) has been adopted for in-car
communication system.
In addition, BCM, ECM, combination meter, P/S control module, ABS control module and SDM transmit / receive data
through a twist pair of two communication lines (CAN High and CAN Low) connected through CAN communication.
Data obtained by a specific control module can be shared with every control module.
CAN Communication Signal
CAN communication system is a serial communication system for transmitting multiple data items (values from
sensors, control data and control signals) as ON/OFF signals through communication lines. This system uses two
lines (CAN High and CAN Low) for the communication circuit so as to maintain high reliability even when used for
high-speed serial communication.
Serial communication is established as shown below with 2.5 V as the reference level for both CAN High signal (1)
and CAN Low signal (2). The range of CAN High signal is from 2.5 V to about 3.5 V and that of CAN Low signal is from
2.5 V to about 1.5 V. When both are at 2.5 V, signal is judged as OFF. When CAN High signal is 3.5 V and CAN Low
signal is 1.5 V (that is, when the difference between High voltage and Low voltage is more than about 2 V), signal is
judged as ON. For this reason, a feature of CAN communication signal is that the signal waveform between CAN High
and CAN Low signals is symmetrical with respect to 2.5 V level. CAN communication fails when the symmetrical
signal form collapses.

CAN Communication System Transmitting and Receiving Data Table
AENBL80AA821003
> **NOTE**
• T (Transmitting): When two or more control modules start transmission at the same time, control
module transmitting the highest priority information enters data transmission mode and all other
control modules enter reception mode.
• R (Receiving): All control modules connected with CAN communication lines receive all information
on CAN communication line. Each control module selects only the necessary information for
performing its control function.
• ECM calculates and determines vehicle speed based on VSS signal and transmits the information to
other control modules through CAN.

Diagnosis Procedure
When “CAN Communication Bus Off” is detected in any control modules, or when it is not possible to communicate
with all control modules / sensor with CAN using SUZUKI scan tool, check the following procedure.

2) Using oscilloscope or oscilloscope function of SUZUKI scan tool, observe waveform in the following condition
when ignition is “ON”.
3) Compare observed signal waveform and waveforms given as “Reference Waveform”. Find the most similar signal
waveform and identify the system in trouble and cause of trouble. )(Page 10H-34)
4) Perform troubleshooting. )(Page 10H-37)

## Halaman 1617 — Section (`Hal-1617`)

Communication System: D13A Model 10H-37
Troubleshooting
> **NOTE**
• Before diagnosing trouble, be sure to check equipment of vehicle being serviced as well as control
modules and sensors connected to CAN communication line.
• Before using scan tool, read its “Operator’s (I nstruction) Manual” to know how to use it.
• When performing “Communication Bus Check” using SUZUKI scan tool in this troubleshooting,
refer to “Judgment of Communication Bus Check”: D13A Model (Page 10H-39).
Step Action Yes No
1 CAN communication circuit check
1) Disconnect negative (–) cable at battery.
2) Disconnect connectors from all the control modules and
sensor communicating by CAN. )(Page 10H-32)
3) Check for proper connection to each CAN
communication circuit at all control module / sensor
(communicating by CAN) connectors and DLC.
4) If connections are OK, check the following points of each
CAN communication circuit based on results found in
Steps 3) of “Diagnosis Procedure”: D13A Model (Page
10H-33).
• Open circuit
• Short to power circuit
• Short to ground circuit
• Short to CAN communication wire with each other
Is check result OK?
Go to Step 2. Repair or replace
defective wire harness.
2 ECM terminating resistance check
1) Connect “E01” connector to ECM.
2) Measure resistance between the following terminals.
• Without ABS: “E04-4” and “E04-11” terminals of BCM
connector
• With ABS: “E24-3” and “E 24-16” terminals of ABS
control module connector
Is resistance 114 to 134 Ω?
Go to Step 3. Replace ECM and
recheck DTC. )(Page
1C-14)
3 Combination meter terminating resistance check
1) Connect connector to combination meter.
2) Measure resistance between “G211-6” and “G211-14”
terminals of DLC.
Is resistance 114 to 134 Ω?
Go to Step 4. Replace combination
meter and recheck
DTC. )(Page 9C-9)
4 Combination meter, P/S control module, BCM, ABS
control module (ABS model) and ECM communication
check
1) Connect connectors to P/S control module, BCM and
ABS control module (ABS model).
2) Connect negative (–) cable at battery.
3) Set ignition “ON”.
4) Select “Communication Bus Check” under “Bus Check”
menu of SUZUKI scan tool.
5) Check that CAN communicatio n is in normal condition
for combination meter, P/S control module, BCM, ABS
control module (ABS model) and ECM. )(Page 10H-39)
Is communication normal?
Perform
“Communication Check”
according to connected
control modules /
sensor. )(Page 10H-
39)
Go to Step 5.

• Between “G50-4” and “G50-5” terminals
• Between “G50-7” and “G50-6” terminals
4) Set ignition “ON”.
5) Select “Communication Bus Check” under “Bus Check”
menu of SUZUKI scan tool.
6) Check that CAN communicatio n is in normal condition
for combination meter, BCM, ABS control module (ABS
model) and ECM. )(Page 10H-39)

Replace P/S control
module and recheck
DTC. )(Page 6C-29)

2) Disconnect service wires from P/S control module
connector, and then connect connector to P/S control
module.
3) Disconnect “G04” and “E04” connectors from BCM.
4) Connect the following terminals of BCM connectors
using service wires.
• Between “G04-2” and “E04-4” terminals
• Between “G04-18” and “E04-11” terminals
5) Set ignition “ON”.
6) Select “Communication Bus Check” under “Bus Check”
menu of SUZUKI scan tool.
7) Check that CAN communicatio n is in normal condition
for combination meter, P/S control module, ABS control
module (ABS model) and ECM. )(Page 10H-39)
Is communication normal?
Replace BCM and
recheck DTC. )(Page

Step 8.
• With ABS: Go to Step
7.

then connect connectors to BCM.

connector using service wires.
• Between “E24-2” and “E24-3” terminals
• Between “E24-15” and “E24-16” terminals
5) Set ignition “ON”.
6) Select “Communication Bus Check” under “Bus Check”
menu of SUZUKI scan tool.
7) Check that CAN communicatio n is in normal condition
for combination meter, P/S control module, BCM and
ECM. )(Page 10H-39)
Is communication normal?
Replace ABS control
module and recheck

## Halaman 1619 — Section (`Hal-1619`)

Communication System: D13A Model 10H-39
Communication Check
SDM (air bag model)
1) Set ignition “OFF”.
2) Connect “G11” connector to SDM.
3) Set ignition “ON”.
4) Select “Communication Bus Check” under “Bus Check” menu of SUZUKI scan tool.
5) Confirm CAN communication that control modules, sensor and SDM which have been already connected are in
normal condition. )(Page 10H-39)
6) If any malfunction is found, replace SDM and recheck DTC. )(Page 8B-61)
Judgment of Communication Bus Check
When performing “Communication Bus Check” using SUZUKI scan tool, refer to the following table for judgment.
8 Combination meter communication check
1) Set ignition “OFF”.
2) Disconnect service wires from connector(s) for the
following control module, and then connect connector(s)
to each control module.
• Without ABS: BCM
• With ABS: ABS control module
3) Replace combination meter. )(Page 9C-9)
4) Set ignition “ON”.
5) Select “Communication Bus Check” under “Bus Check”
menu of SUZUKI scan tool.
6) Check that CAN communicatio n is in normal condition
for combination meter, P/S control module, BCM, ABS
control module (ABS model) and ECM. )(Page 10H-39)
Is communication normal?
End. (Combination
meter was faulty.)
Replace ECM and
recheck DTC. )(Page
1C-14)
Step Action Yes No
Judgment Display of Communication Bus Check
Normal
• All connected control modules / sensor (communicating by CAN) are displayed and its
back ground color is “White”.
• Above state remains unchanged while monitoring for longer than 1 minute.
Abnormal
• Even one of connected control modules / sensor (communicating by CAN) is not
displayed.
• Background color for names of control modu les / sensor (communicating by CAN) is
displayed in “Gray” or “Light blue”.
• Background color for names of control modu les / sensor (communicating by CAN) is
changed to “Gray” (the numbers of control modules / sensors decrease) or “Light blue”
(the numbers of control modules / sensor increase).
• “Communication Bus Check” cannot be executed.
